subject: Post-demo: throughput dimensioning & dedicated validation plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@circuitmd.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-09-28T15:10:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: throughput dimensioning & dedicated validation plan

Hi Rajiv / Lena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the validation run: 

- Goal: validate Dedicated reserved throughput and SLOs for your real-time clinical summarization use case (P95 latency target <= 120ms for 512-token streaming responses; sustained throughput target ~140 qps with burst headroom to 220 qps).
- Primary workload characteristics you confirmed: concurrent interactive sessions ~60–80 during peak, average request size ~400 tokens, ~15% of requests are long-streaming (>1s).
- Quality bar: production rollout needs parity with your current on-prem baseline (you provided example traces). We’ll include those as baseline in the run.

What we’ll validate in the Dedicated trial:
1) Latency P95/P99 at your concurrency and throughput targets (streaming enabled).
2) End-to-end tail behavior when KV cache hits vs cold-cache.
3) Cost & throughput per reserved GPU type (A100-40GB, H100-80GB, L4) mapped to your request mix.
4) Failure/fallback behaviour: model-variant fallback and cross-region spillover (optional).

Proposed validation plan (short):
- We’ll provision a Reserved pool for a 72-hour validation window.
- Run three controlled load profiles (low/med/high) using your traces + synthetic augmentation.
- Observability: per-token latency, cost/token estimate, GPU utilization, and trace-level clips for any failed streams.

Attachments: I’ve dropped a short eval plan + sample trace format (circuitmd-eval-plan.xlsx, sample-traces-20260928.jsonl).

Next steps: please confirm the validation window you prefer (we can start as early as next week), and confirm whether you want us to include H100 in the initial run (adds higher perf but procurement lead time is longer).

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0134

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@circuitmd.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@circuitmd.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-09-28T18:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput dimensioning & dedicated validation plan

Jonas — thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side that should shape the run: 

- The 140 qps sustained is our target for the US-East cluster only (we’ll have a smaller EU cluster later). Peak concurrency of 60–80 is accurate but note that bursts can spike to ~240 qps for 20–30s when shift changes occur.
- For latency: our product team will accept P95 <= 120ms, but P99 cannot exceed 350ms during normal operating windows.
- KV cache hit rate expected ~55% on warm runs; cold-cache scenarios happen at the start of every hour due to rotation.
- Model: we plan to serve a 7B/13B open-weights variant (you called it ‘med-llm’ during the demo). Provide mapping to quantized variants if latency improves.

We are interested in H100 if the perf delta vs A100 justifies the price. L4 could be interesting for cost-optimized background jobs but unsure about streaming tails.

We can approve a 72-hour window the week of Oct 5. Please send an exact calendar invite and an endpoint for our load generator to push traces.

—Rajiv
CTO, CircuitMD
rajiv@circuitmd.com

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@circuitmd.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T09:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput dimensioning & dedicated validation plan

Thanks Rajiv — noted. Internal note / plan for validation run: 

- Hardware matrix to test (each compared against CircuitMD traces):
  * 2x A100-40GB nodes (reserved pool) — baseline perf/cost
  * 1x H100-80GB node (reserved) — high-perf, lower latency tails (estimate lower P95 by ~20–30% for streaming workloads)
  * 4x L4 (edge/cheap) — cost-per-qps baseline for non-streaming or batch summarization

- Sizing heuristics: start with config that provides ~180 qps headroom on A100 pool (to accommodate 220 spikes), collect GPU util and latency curves. If P99 tail > 350ms at high spike, escalate to H100 run.
- Streaming config: enable small chunk streaming (32-token chunks), KV prefetch for warm-hit runs. Measure per-chunk latency and reassemble overhead.
- Metrics to capture: P50/P95/P99 latency (streaming & finalization), tokens/sec per GPU, GPU memory residency, KV hit ratio, and cold-start penalty.

Action items: Marcus to prepare the load harness connectors and we’ll need CircuitMD’s trace upload (sample-traces already included). Jonas — can you confirm reserved pool sizes & tentative start date Oct 5 and create DocuSign PO stub if they want a short-term reserved contract?

-Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>

Rajiv / Lena — all set on our side for Oct 5 launch. Summary of confirmed items and immediate asks: 

- Validation window: Oct 5 08:00 UTC — Oct 8 08:00 UTC (72 hours).
- Hardware we’ll stand up initially: 2x A100-40GB (reserved pool); we’ll keep H100 on standby for escalation (Marcus: please provision H100 slot but don’t activate).
- Action from CircuitMD: upload final trace bundle to the Drive link and share any authentication details for the load generator by EOD Oct 1.
- PO / procurement: I’ll send a short-term reserved PO template (DocuSign link) for the 72-hour evaluation; pricing will be preliminary and credited if you convert to a 3mo reserved contract.

I’ve attached the evaluation workbook (circuitmd-eval-plan.xlsx) with test profiles and expected KPIs — Marcus will reach out with the load generator endpoint and runbook.

Proposed calendar invite will follow. Thanks — excited to get this validated.

Jonas
